context.body: After this, David struck the Philistines and subdued them; and David took the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Campaigns against Philistines, Moab, Hadadezer, Syria, Edom, and others bring tribute and dedicated objects; the chapter closes with justice, officials, and David’s sons.
observations.label: Victories, tribute, dedication, and administration: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, defeated peoples, Toi, Joab, officials, and Israel, Philistia, Moab, Zobah, Syria, Edom, Jerusalem, and the kingdom, defeating, measuring, hamstringing, garrisoning, receiving tribute, dedicating, ruling, and appointing visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Victories, tribute, dedication, and administration: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, defeated peoples, Toi, Joab, officials, and Israel · Philistia, Moab, Zobah, Syria, Edom, Jerusalem, and the kingdom · defeating, measuring, hamstringing, garrisoning, receiving tribute, dedicating, ruling, and appointing · military expansion and administrative order are narrated together
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 8:1–18

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 8:1–18 as its own ark, house, and kingdom David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places military expansion and administrative order are narrated together inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
